solution: A frequency polygon is drawn by joining the mid-points of the tops of the rectangles of a histogram, so the histogram is drawn first.
An ogive is a cumulative frequency curve. Reading off the value at half the total frequency gives the median (and similarly the quartiles).
The gap between one class's upper limit and the next class's lower limit is 1, so half of it, 0.5, is subtracted from each lower limit: 9.5, 19.5, 29.5 and 39.5.
The mean of the five is \(\frac{5x + 20}{5} = x + 4 = 11\), so \(x = 7\). The first three are 7, 9, 11, whose mean is \(\frac{27}{3} = 9\).
All 10 items total \(12 \times 10 = 120\). The first two groups (5 items) total \(3 \times 5 = 15\). The third group's 5 items total \(120 - 15 = 105\), so its mean is \(\frac{105}{5} = 21\).
Combined mean \(= \frac{7 \times 10 + 3 \times 5}{7 + 3} = \frac{85}{10} = 8.5\).
The 10 who failed scored \(10 \times 28 = 280\). The 40 who passed scored \(2800 - 280 = 2520\), an average of \(\frac{2520}{40} = 63\).

The median depends only on the middle position, so extreme values do not affect it, it can be found when the end items are unknown as long as their number is known, and it can be used for data that can be ranked but not measured (such as intelligence). All three statements are true.
The middle item of a series arranged in order of size is the median.
108 marks out of 540 is \(\frac{108}{540} = \frac{1}{5}\) of the total, which takes \(\frac{1}{5} \times 360^\circ = 72^\circ\) of the chart. The \(72^\circ\) sector is Social Science.

Each value \(\frac{1}{k}\) occurs \(k\) times, so each contributes \(k \times \frac{1}{k} = 1\) and \(\sum fx = n\). The total frequency is \(1 + 2 + \ldots + n = \frac{n(n + 1)}{2}\). Mean \(= \frac{n}{n(n + 1)/2} = \frac{2}{n + 1}\).
The geometric mean of three numbers is the cube root of their product: \(40 \times 50 \times x = 10^3 = 1000\), so \(2000x = 1000\) and \(x = \frac{1}{2}\).

The sum of the deviations from the arithmetic mean, each weighted by its frequency, is always zero: \(\sum f_i(X_i - \mu) = \sum f_i X_i - \mu \sum f_i = 0\), because \(\mu = \frac{\sum f_i X_i}{\sum f_i}\).

In a histogram it is the AREA of each rectangle that is proportional to the class frequency. The height is proportional to the frequency only when all classes have the same width, so the statement about the height of the bar is not correct in general. The other three statements are true.

District A's modal class is 44.0-47.0 (59 plots): mode \(= 44 + \frac{59 - 36}{2 \times 59 - 36 - 30} \times 3 = 44 + \frac{23}{52} \times 3 \approx 45.33\). District B's modal class is 47.0-50.0 (54 plots): mode \(= 47 + \frac{54 - 35}{2 \times 54 - 35 - 41} \times 3 = 47 + \frac{19}{32} \times 3 \approx 48.78\). The mode for district B is higher.
The recorded total is \(50 \times 44 = 2200\). Replacing 73 by 23 lowers it by 50, to 2150. The correct average is \(\frac{2150}{50} = 43\).
A 'less than' cumulative frequency counts the items below a class's upper limit, so it is plotted against the upper limit of each class.

By the empirical relation, mode \(= 3 \times\) median \(- 2 \times\) mean \(= 3 \times 9 - 2 \times 8.9 = 27 - 17.8 = 9.2\).

Adding \(k\) to every number adds \(k\) to the arithmetic mean, the median and the mid-range. The geometric mean does not shift this way: for 1 and 4 it is 2, but for 2 and 5 (each increased by 1) it is \(\sqrt{10} \ne 3\).
There are 10 numbers, so the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th: \(\frac{9 + x}{2} = 10\), giving \(x = 11\), which keeps the list in ascending order.
Ten classes of width 2.5 span \(10 \times 2.5 = 25\), so the upper boundary of the highest class is \(5.1 + 25 = 30.1\).
2, 8, 3, 7, 4, 6, 7 in order is 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 7, 8, with median 6. In 2, 9, 3, 4, 9, 6, 9 the value 9 occurs most, so the mode is 9. Their average is \(\frac{6 + 9}{2} = 7.5\).
Let the mean be \(m\). Subtracting 10 from each value gives mean \(m - 10 = 0.6m\), so \(m = 25\). Adding 5 to each value gives mean \(25 + 5 = 30\).
The range is \(120 - 71 = 49\); seven classes give a width of \(\frac{49}{7} = 7\). In ascending order the classes are 71-78, 78-85, 85-92, ..., 113-120, so the second class has limits 78 and 85.

\(\frac{1}{2}\left(y + \frac{1}{y}\right) = M\), so \(y + \frac{1}{y} = 2M\). Then \(y^3 + \frac{1}{y^3} = \left(y + \frac{1}{y}\right)^3 - 3\left(y + \frac{1}{y}\right) = 8M^3 - 6M\). Their mean is \(\frac{8M^3 - 6M}{2} = M(4M^2 - 3)\).
The modal class is 15-20 (frequency 80). Mode \(= 15 + \frac{80 - 30}{2 \times 80 - 30 - 40} \times 5 = 15 + \frac{50}{90} \times 5 \approx 17.78\), so \(15 < m < 20\).
India's square has area \(\frac{81}{25} = 3.24 \text{ cm}^2\), so its side is \(\sqrt{3.24} = 1.8\) cm.

Motorola's share is \(\frac{3}{3 + 5 + 8} = \frac{3}{16}\), so its angle is \(\frac{3}{16} \times 360^\circ = 67.5^\circ\). The total number of phones is not needed.
Statistical data are numerical facts collected for a purpose and comparable with one another. Monthly rainfall volumes over 24 months are such data; lists of names are not.

The first seven primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17: mean \(\frac{58}{7} \approx 8.29\), median 7, so Statement I is true. Statement II is false: the mean is not always greater than the median (for the first two primes, 2 and 3, both are 2.5, and for a set such as 1, 9, 10 the mean is below the median). So Only I.

A histogram is a set of adjacent vertical rectangles on a common base with no gaps between them, and each rectangle's height is set by the frequency of its class (for classes of equal width). Both statements are correct.
A histogram represents the whole frequency distribution, and it suits a continuous variable because each class's frequency is drawn as if spread evenly across the class. Both statements are correct.

Primary data are collected first-hand by the investigator: door-to-door visits (I) and telephone interviews (III). Figures taken from census records (II) were collected by someone else, so they are secondary data.
For collar sizes the useful figure is the size that sells most, which is the mode. Marks are summarised by the mean and incomes, which are skewed, by the median.

A straight cumulative frequency line means every class has the same frequency, \(\frac{60}{6} = 10\). So I is true; the two middle classes total \(10 + 10 = 20\), not 30, so II is false; and with all frequencies equal there is no mode, so III is true.
For the mode to be 1, its frequency 6 must be the largest, so \(x < 6\) (at \(x = 6\) both 1 and 3 would be modes). The largest possible value is 5.

The cumulative frequencies are 3, 9, 11 for 0, 1, 2 goals, and \(n = 16 + x\). At \(x = 2\), \(n = 18\) and the median is the mean of the 9th and 10th values, 1 and 2, which is 1.5. At \(x = 3\), \(n = 19\) and the median is the 10th value, which is 2. So the smallest \(x\) is 3.
The total is \(6 + 7 + 3 + 4 + 2.5 + 1.5 = 24\) lakh. The largest item, 7 lakh, gets \(\frac{7}{24} \times 360^\circ = 105^\circ\).
Of the 24 lakh total, the largest item (7) gets \(105^\circ\) and the smallest (1.5) gets \(\frac{1.5}{24} \times 360^\circ = 22.5^\circ\). The difference is \(82.5^\circ\).
The median 20 lies in class 18-23 (frequency 40), with \(7 + x\) bulbs before it: \(18 + \frac{50 - (7 + x)}{40} \times 5 = 20\), so \(\frac{43 - x}{8} = 2\) and \(x = 27\).
The median condition \(18 + \frac{50 - (7 + x)}{40} \times 5 = 20\) gives \(x = 27\). The total is 100: \(7 + 27 + 40 + y + 10 + 2 = 100\), so \(y = 14\).

The median of \(a, a, b, b, c, c\) is \(b = 2\). The mean gives \(\frac{2(a + b + c)}{6} = \frac{7}{3}\), so \(a + c = 5\). The geometric mean gives \((abc)^{1/3} = 2\), so \(ac = 4\). Hence \(a = 1\), \(c = 4\), and the sum of squares is \(2(1 + 4 + 16) = 42\).
The median gives \(b = 2\); the mean gives \(a + b + c = 7\), so \(a + c = 5\); the geometric mean gives \(abc = 8\), so \(ac = 4\). With \(a < c\), \(a = 1\) and \(c = 4\).

The numbers are 1, 1, 2, 2, 4, 4 (from \(b = 2\), \(a + c = 5\) and \(ac = 4\)). Every value occurs exactly twice, so no value occurs more often than the others and the data have no mode. None of these.
Wheat has \(70^\circ\) of \(360^\circ\): \(\frac{70}{360} \times 100\% \approx 19.44\%\).
Sugar's \(40^\circ\) stands for 9000 kg, so wheat's \(70^\circ\) stands for \(9000 \times \frac{70}{40} = 15750\) kg.
Wheat and sugar differ by \(70^\circ - 40^\circ = 30^\circ\), which is \(\frac{30}{360} \times 180000 = 15000\) kg.
The total is 100, so the median is the 50th value. The cumulative frequencies are 6, 36, 76, so it lies in 7-10: median \(= 7 + \frac{50 - 36}{40} \times 3 = 7 + 1.05 = 8.05\).
The modal class is 7-10 (frequency 40): mode \(= 7 + \frac{40 - 30}{2 \times 40 - 30 - 16} \times 3 = 7 + \frac{10}{34} \times 3 \approx 7.88\).
